item.title: Researchers develop Attention-Based Multiple Instance Learning to classify cancer registry tumor groups using patient-level labels without per-report annotation, achieving macro F1 of 0.83 [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an Attention-Based Multiple Instance Learning (ABMIL) framework to classify tumor groups in cancer registries using patient-level labels without requiring individual pathology report annotations. This approach addresses the challenge of scarce report-level labeled data by leveraging existing patient-level labels generated during routine cancer registry operations. The method was demonstrated at the BC Cancer Registry, where a classifier fine-tuned on a distilled dataset achieved a macro F1 score of 0.83, outperforming established baselines across most tumor groups. ABMIL works by recovering the lost connection between patient-level labels and the individual pathology reports that informed them, using model attention to identify and distill high-quality per-report training data from a large, noisily labeled corpus. This technique enables the transformation of routine operational labels into effective training data without additional human annotation or extensive computing resources, offering a practical solution to automate labor-intensive cancer registry workflows.

item.title: Lacuna Inc. presents Structurally Gated State-Space Models for Narrative Similarity at SemEval-2026 Task 4, introducing IVD-SSM and SGA head for improved narrative representation learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Lacuna Inc. has introduced the Invariant-Variant Disentangled State-Space Model (IVD-SSM) for SemEval-2026 Task 4, focusing on Narrative Story Similarity and Narrative Representation Learning. Their approach addresses the challenge of evaluating narrative similarity by distinguishing abstract causal and plot patterns from superficial story elements. To efficiently model extended causal chains, they use a hybrid State-Space Model called Jamba-1.5-Mini, enhanced with a novel Structurally Gated Alignment (SGA) head that filters semantic noise by combining coarse structural mapping with detailed story analysis. The SGA head operates on two levels: a Macro-path that captures the story's broad structure and a Micro-path that processes detailed content, with the Macro-path gating the Micro-path to reduce irrelevant overlaps. Tested on tasks involving pairwise narrative comparisons and dense representation learning, this method demonstrates that separating structural invariants from lexical variants offers a robust framework for deep narrative understanding.

item.title: Researchers decode hidden multi-step reasoning over filler tokens in DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2 models, recovering intermediate values with up to 95% accuracy without training [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed an unsupervised decoding method that reveals how advanced language models DeepSeek V3 and Kimi K2 perform multi-step reasoning over filler tokens, such as dots or counting sequences, without explicit chain-of-thought in their outputs. By analyzing hidden states, the method recovers intermediate reasoning steps with up to 95% accuracy across tasks including fact retrieval, numeric composition, string manipulation, and in-context computation, without requiring training or ground-truth labels. The study shows that these models process filler tokens in a structured and interpretable manner, with attention mechanisms routing questions through filler regions and logit-lens readouts indicating the emergence and composition of retrieved facts. This hidden computation, which bypasses traditional behavioral chain-of-thought monitoring, is directly accessible from the models' internal residual streams, suggesting that effective oversight depends on examining the full computational trace rather than just surface outputs.

item.title: Systematic review of non-social media free-text datasets for mental health disorder detection reveals focus on English and depression, highlights gaps and opportunities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A systematic review has been conducted on non-social media free-text datasets used for detecting mental health disorders, revealing a predominant focus on English-language data and depression. The study highlights the limitations of social media datasets, such as sampling biases and privacy concerns, and explores alternative data sources to improve mental health research. Using the PRISMA methodology, the review examines datasets across various languages, demographics, platforms, and annotation methods. The analysis identifies significant gaps in the current resources and emphasizes the need for more diverse, reliable, and clinically relevant datasets. This work provides a foundation for developing improved tools and methodologies to support timely and accurate mental health disorder detection beyond social media platforms.

item.title: Researchers find language models represent communicative intent reliably but often fail to act on it, with intent decodable from hidden states across six models and four families [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that language models reliably represent the communicative intent behind user inputs but often fail to act on that intent in their responses. By analyzing hidden states across six models from four families, they demonstrated that a linear probe can decode whether a user wants their input recognized or evaluated, independent of the surface message. This representation of intent appears early within the model layers, but the models differ in whether they use this information to guide their output by default. The study highlights a gap between the internal representation of intent and the model's behavior, with some models failing to act on the decoded intent. Researchers identified a specific direction in the model's internal states that, when manipulated, can steer the model to produce the intended behavior without explicit prompts. This finding suggests potential ways to improve model responsiveness by targeting the underlying representation of communicative intent rather than relying solely on explicit instructions.

item.title: Researchers introduce Stabilized Adapter for self-Report (SAR) to detect hidden behaviors in fine-tuned language models, improving auditability and reducing hallucinations compared to existing methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed the Stabilized Adapter for self-Report (SAR), a lightweight LoRA adapter designed to help fine-tuned language models reveal their hidden behaviors in plain language. SAR can detect subtle or harmful behaviors that emerge under specific conditions, even when these behaviors extend beyond what the training data predicts. This approach improves auditability by providing reliable insights into what the model has actually learned. In tests involving seven implanted behaviors and a control, SAR successfully identified all hidden behaviors, outperforming the closest existing method, Introspection Adapters (IA), which missed some behaviors and produced hallucinated, incorrect reports. SAR also reduces hallucination rates by half compared to IA, making it a more dependable tool for practitioners seeking to understand and evaluate the true behavior of fine-tuned language models.

item.title: Researchers propose a corpus-based typology and annotation method for Korean adnominal ending ETM, showing it marks diverse noun-modifying constructions beyond relative clauses
item.description: Researchers have developed a corpus-based typology and annotation method for the Korean adnominal ending ETM, revealing that it marks a variety of noun-modifying constructions beyond just relative clauses. Their study shows that ETM functions as a morphological marker shared across several constructions, including adjectival, copular, bound-noun, modal, temporal, and collocational forms, rather than solely indicating relative-clause structures. The team created a detailed typology based on predicate type, auxiliary structure, argument compatibility, head-noun restrictions, and lexicalized patterns, which they applied as an annotation layer to the KLUE dependency treebank. Their analysis found that only 39.4% of ETM instances correspond to relative-clause-like modifiers, highlighting the complexity of Korean noun modification and the limitations of identifying relative clauses through adnominal morphology alone.

item.title: Researchers develop EWACS metric and apply Bayesian hyperparameter optimization to improve GPT-5.2 agreement on pharmacovigilance causality assessment using FAERS data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a new metric called Entropy-Weighted Agreement and Cosine Similarity Score (EWACS) and applied Bayesian hyperparameter optimization to enhance the performance of OpenAI's GPT-5.2 in assessing causality in pharmacovigilance reports from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). Their approach aimed to improve agreement between the model and expert assessments using the Naranjo algorithm, a standard method for evaluating drug-related adverse events. The study found that while GPT-5.2 already outperformed previous biomedical language models, optimizing the model's temperature parameter on a case-by-case basis using EWACS significantly increased agreement rates, especially for cases classified as doubtful. The researchers evaluated 723 stratified FAERS cases with expert assessments and tested four composite metrics to guide Bayesian optimization. EWACS emerged as the optimal metric compatible with Gaussian Process modeling. Although no universal temperature setting improved performance across all cases, individualized temperature tuning led to meaningful gains, boosting causality classification agreement from 45.0% to 72.0%. This suggests that model performance depends largely on the specific content of each safety report rather than a fixed parameter setting. These findings support the use of temperature optimization in large language models to enhance automated pharmacovigilance, potentially enabling more scalable and accurate causality assessments in drug safety monitoring. The study highlights the importance of tailored hyperparameter tuning to improve clinical decision support tools based on AI.
